objections.label: STARDUST quadrupling kills the hobby tier
objections.steelman: The cheapest tier exists for tinkerers and side projects, and it just went from negligible to noticeable in one move. Two separate voices in a 16-post run independently center the same 4x figure, and the hobbyist segment has the lowest switching friction of any cohort — they leave quietly and never come back.
objections.threatenedDecision: Raising STARDUST1-S 4x without a hobbyist carve-out.

objections.label: No exit path disclosed
objections.steelman: Across three rounds nobody answers what leaving costs — no portability terms, no migration help, no egress discussion. A price rise without an exit reads as confidence that customers are stuck, and that reading hardens faster than any table justifies.
objections.threatenedDecision: Publishing the increase with zero portability language.

objections.label: Partnership framing invites cynicism
objections.steelman: The announcement asks to be read as partners sharing realities, but offers no vote, no opt-out, and no grandfathering. Readers experience the gap between the framing and the mechanism directly, and the most engaged post in the run is the one naming it.
objections.threatenedDecision: Leading with partnership language instead of plain terms.

objections.label: GPU hike hits fixed-budget AI teams
objections.steelman: A 10% rise on H100 hourly rates lands on teams with fixed compute budgets mid-runway, where there is no slack to absorb it. The engagement concentrates here because the pain is arithmetic, not sentiment.
objections.threatenedDecision: Applying the increase to GPU lines without a reservation bridge.

objections.label: Serverless doubling punishes unpredictability
objections.steelman: Doubling per-GB-second memory pricing hits exactly the workloads chosen for cost control — bursty, spiky, hard to forecast. Those users cannot budget the new rate, so they must either over-provision or leave.
objections.threatenedDecision: Doubling serverless memory rates without a cap or estimator.

strongestCritic.sentence: Precision without an exit and partnership without a vote is just a well-formatted bill.

draft.counterCase: Three years of flat prices while hardware costs went vertical is a real record, and the ~2% lines on core compute genuinely track input inflation rather than margin-taking. The run's own measured voice concedes this, and one committed supporter holds the line in public. A targeted increase that funds capacity beats the alternative of degraded service or a panicked blanket hike later.

weakestClaim.claim: Customers will read the detailed table as transparency rather than as a bill.
weakestClaim.breakingQuestion: Show three customers the table with no preamble — do any of them use the word transparent unprompted?

testPlan.question: What would make this price acceptable to you?
testPlan.discriminates: Whether the objection is the number or the surprise.
testPlan.wouldNotShipIf: Most respondents name a lower number rather than better communication.

testPlan.question: If you left over this, where would you go and what stops you today?
testPlan.discriminates: Whether lock-in or price is the binding constraint.
testPlan.wouldNotShipIf: Nobody can name a viable alternative, meaning the hike is safe but the resentment compounds.

testPlan.question: Which single line item would you cut from the increase to keep us?
testPlan.discriminates: Whether pain concentrates on outliers or spreads across the table.
testPlan.wouldNotShipIf: Everyone names the same two outliers, meaning a targeted rollback saves the launch.
